title: Chapter 3 — Home Front
description: A teacher can't campaign from a classroom. A daughter can't hide from her father's posters. A wife's landlord has heard you're rich now.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Monday. Iyana-Wahala Community Secondary School. Your JSS 2 class has drawn your campaign poster on the blackboard, with a crown.

beats.speaker: principal
beats.text: Mr. {name}. (Mrs. Bánkọ́lé, the principal, closes the door.) Civil servants cannot be candidates. You must resign, or take leave without pay. The Ministry is already asking.

beats.speaker: principal
beats.text: Eleven years. The best civics teacher I have. (She sighs.) Don't make me sign your exit letter, please.

beats.speaker: principal
beats.text: Your class is singing your jingle outside the door. Badly.

options.text: Take leave without pay. Keep the door open.
Withdraw from the race. The classroom is enough.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You walk back into JSS 2. You wipe the crown off the blackboard. You teach the Constitution, chapter four: fundamental rights. Thirty-eight children listen like it's news.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: (that evening, with jollof, the good one) I was ready for the election. I'm more ready for this. (She puts more meat on your plate than the recipe allows.)

beats.title: The Classroom
beats.summary: You stepped off the ballot and back to the blackboard. In twenty years, one of your students runs for councillor. She wins clean. She tells the newspapers who taught her.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Evening. Your daughter Tolú, fifteen, comes home with her school shirt torn at the pocket.

beats.speaker: tolu
beats.text: They put your poster in the girls' toilet. With a moustache. Some boy said you will steal like the rest. I hit him. (She lifts her chin.) I'm not sorry.

beats.speaker: tolu
beats.text: She is waiting to see which father you will be.

options.text: "Hitting is wrong. But tell me what he said, exactly."
"Maybe he's right to worry. Ask me anything. I'll tell you the truth."

beats.speaker: tolu
beats.text: (She thinks.) Okay. Did Baba Oko give you money? (She waits.) ...You took a long time. That's an answer, Daddy.

variants.text: (She thinks.) Okay. Did Baba Oko give you money? ...No? (She looks at you hard, then smiles.) Okay. I believe you. Barely.

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: The landlord of my shop came today. Rent is now ₦240,000, not ₦120,000. Because my husband is "a politician now". (She folds a wrapper too hard.)

beats.speaker: funke
beats.text: Her shop. Twelve years at a table, two years with a door.

options.text: Go and see the landlord yourself. Politely. With a lawyer's letterhead.
Pay the difference from campaign money. Just this once.

variants.text: (Later.) He reduced it back. He said, "I didn't know Teacher was so... legal." (She laughs.) Neither did I.
"After the election." (She writes it on a piece of paper and sticks it on the fridge.) I am collecting your promises. For the museum.

beats.title: Home Front
beats.summary: A classroom you may not see again, a daughter who fights for you, and a landlord who discovered politics. Campaigns start at home.
